chunks: Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
Any man who acknowledges his child and then later disowns him has no right to do that, and no dignity in it. His child is to be attributed to him if the child is from his wife or his maidservant.

key_terms.أَقَرَّ بِوَلَدِهِ: formally acknowledged his child as his own
key_terms.يُلْحَقُ بِهِ وَلَدُهُ: his child is legally affiliated and attributed to him

ai.seo_question: Can a father disown a child after previously acknowledging him in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that a man who has acknowledged his child cannot later deny the child's affiliation to him. If the child is born from his wife or his maidservant, the child's lineage remains attached to him.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5680 - Hammad narrated from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:

"Any man who acknowledges his child and then later denies him has no right to do so, and he deserves no respect.
His child will be attributed to him if the child is from his wife or his maidservant."
